subject.title: feat(workspace): lint and auto-fix code fences in markdown at write time

question: Should OpenClaw add Markdown code-fence linting to workspace writes, and if so should the default be auto-fix, warn-only, or explicit opt-in?
rationale: The request mutates persisted workspace Markdown and adds config/API surface, while prior PR review found parser edge cases that could corrupt real documents; automation cannot choose that policy safely.

options.title: Opt-In Or Warn-First Lint
options.body: Add a parser-backed warning or explicit opt-in fix mode first, keeping existing writes unchanged by default while maintainers evaluate false positives.

options.title: Default Auto-Fix
options.body: Rewrite workspace Markdown on write by default, accepting higher compatibility and content-mutation risk for stronger formatting guarantees.

options.title: No Core Write-Time Mutation
options.body: Keep core writes raw and rely on docs linting, prompts, or external tooling unless a narrower runtime bug proves a core hook is needed.

recommendation.title: Opt-In Or Warn-First Lint
recommendation.body: Add a parser-backed warning or explicit opt-in fix mode first, keeping existing writes unchanged by default while maintainers evaluate false positives.

likelyOwner.reason: The likely decision is in core workspace write behavior and current history points to this owner path.
